top_3_bounce_moments.moment: Admin/returning-user dashboard is a red-alert wall of shame
top_3_bounce_moments.detail: On admin login the landing view auto-selects the last-used project 'aurem-demo/frontend' which is marked 'repo unreachable'. The user is greeted by (a) a red 'GitHub access revoked — reconnect to keep chatting' banner, (b) a yellow '12 projects point to deleted or unreachable repos — click to clean up' banner, (c) a floating '2 console errors — SEND TO ORA →' badge, and (d) an 'ORA GUIDE — frontend looks disconnected from GitHub — use the switcher above' tooltip. Four different warnings at once on the very first paint feels broken/abandoned. A real returning user would think the product is down. Suggest: collapse into one 'Reconnect' hero card, or auto-suppress banners when the switcher already shows the project as unreachable.

top_3_bounce_moments.moment: Fresh user sees an ORA-GUIDE bubble that mislabels the CTA
top_3_bounce_moments.detail: On brand-new-account dashboard, the ORA-GUIDE tooltip says 'Connect your repo to get started — click Connect GitHub above.' But the actual visible button in the banner is labeled 'Connect repo →' (not 'Connect GitHub'). Small label mismatch, but for a first-timer scanning the screen it costs a beat of 'wait, which one?'. Also the tooltip anchors bottom-right and overlaps the Advisor rail, so clicking 'Got it' is fine but the visual competes with the Advisor tab tag.

top_3_bounce_moments.moment: Two send-looking controls in the chat area — 'SEND TO ORA →' badge vs the real chat-send
top_3_bounce_moments.detail: The composer has the real send button ([data-testid=chat-send], icon-only, bottom-right of textarea). But the top-right of the chat pane has a much more prominent orange text button 'SEND TO ORA →' ([data-testid=f12-badge-send-action]) which actually forwards the on-page console errors to ORA — not the user's typed message. During automated testing this button was picked up first by substring 'send'. A first-time user with a message typed would almost certainly click the prominent 'SEND TO ORA →' first and be confused when their prompt doesn't leave the textarea. Suggest: rename it to 'Report console errors' or move it out of the immediate composer visual zone; put the real chat send in a labelled pill.
